meta.title: 5 Stoic rules for when life falls apart

Caspar David Friedrich Two Men Contemplating the Moon

beats.text: Five Stoic rules for when everything is falling apart.
One. Divide the situation in two: what you control, and what you don't. Then drop the second half.
Two. The event isn't what hurts you. The story you wrap around it does. See it plainly first.
Three. Act from your values, not your mood. Do the next right thing even when you don't feel like it.
Four. Remember that nothing is permanent — and that includes this. The storm is also passing.
Five. Ask one question: what would the best version of me do in the next ten minutes?
You can't choose the storm. You can always choose how you meet it.

source_note: Inspired by Marcus Aurelius, Seneca & Epictetus.
